setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named three times across the call by both parties: 'I'm sure Kim has probably mentioned a few details to you'; 'I forgot the details to Kim'; and at the disqualification, 'it's not Kim's fault, it's not anyone's fault, it's just, it is what it is.'

prospect.name: Atul Sharma
prospect.occupation: Engineer, works from home; desk-bound roughly six to seven hours from 5am to around noon
prospect.training_background: Wrestled at high school and competed at state level. Lived in India for some years, wrestling and training with steel mace. CrossFit background, so has existing kettlebell competence — swings, snatches, get-ups. Boxing for three and a half to four years, competing in the Masters division with his last bout in February; spars hard and regularly. Currently trains around seven times a week: boxing Monday and Friday mornings, a five-day bro split Monday to Friday, and a weekend run or a self-selected 20-minute YouTube kettlebell workout. Has lost six to eight pounds over two to three months and is starting to see visible abs.
prospect.medical: Chronic stiffness and pain in the lower back, hips and shoulders, described as lifelong — 'It's always been the case.' Under chiropractic care: 'All my chiropractors say I'm the stiffest guy that I've ever met.' Shoulders fatigue during high-volume boxing. No other conditions disclosed and none asked about.

signals: Self-directed, capable, and his own approach is currently working — six to eight pounds down in two to three months with visible abs on a diet he designed himself
Explicitly wants only the programming and refuses the rest: 'I don't need a lot of handholding, right? I just need a program that I can do. I'm disciplined enough to kind of go through it.'
Already using the free substitute successfully — 'I'll pick up a kettlebell and just go to YouTube and do a 20-minute workout'
Named a hard budget and treated the decision as a budget allocation, not a value question: 'It's not about the worth. It's my budget.'
Asked directly for a discount — 'Do you guys have any promotions coming up? Father's Day or whatever is coming up next month?'
Stated the fallback plainly: 'if it doesn't work out, that's what I'll probably end up doing, is going by itself'
Overlaps heavily with the_optimizer on profile — fit, disciplined, 7/10 wanting 10/10 — but diverges on the criterion that defines it, since price was an absolute barrier rather than a quality signal

goals.text: Get a structured, refreshing kettlebell programme he can follow five to six days a week without thinking
Build athleticism for boxing — spar six to ten rounds without being winded, with explosiveness between rounds
Improve mobility and reduce stiffness in lower back, hips and shoulders
Train functionally rather than as a 'gym bro' — movement with purpose rather than pushing weight
Build a training approach that still works at 55, not just at 45
Have the energy to play with his two children whenever they want, not only when he feels up to it
Get from a self-rated seven out of ten to a ten, because he is 'wired that way'

pains.text: Lifelong stiffness and pain in the lower back, hips and shoulders, worsened by six hours seated a day
Shoulders fatigue during long boxing rounds, limiting him to three or four hard rounds before needing rest
Gym training has become boring and he does not believe it serves his goals
No mobility work in his routine at all, and his gym split isolates muscles rather than integrating movement
Aware that pushing weight will not sustain him into his fifties — 'at 45, I'm fine. What's going to happen at 55?'
Lacks a structured kettlebell programme and is currently improvising from YouTube
Energy drops in the evening after 4.30am starts
Family and children absorb most of the discretionary budget

objections.raw_quote: To be honest, it's Steve, I was looking at a couple of hundred bucks a month type thing, right? 150 was, was thinking, I'm looking for somebody with a programming, right?... In fact, my one-on-one coaching and boxing is nowhere close to this, you know, which is with personal trainer at the, right? So it's definitely, it's way out of my range from what I was thinking
objections.rep_response: Did not attempt to close the gap. Disqualified the prospect — 'If you were to really, like, put gun to my head, I don't really think you need the one-on-one coaching like that' — and pivoted to a $200 per month product, Primal University, which he demonstrated by screen share.

objections.raw_quote: the biggest pillar that I'm interested in is the pillar one, right? Two and three, I'm not so much... I have the whole nutrition things customized for me already from there. Accountability, I'm pretty headstrong, so I'm good on accountability and I'm not a very social person about communities and stuff. So I'm straight on. So pillar one is what I'm looking for
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged it with 'Cool, man' and moved directly to the alignment question. Later used it as part of the rationale for the downsell.

objections.raw_quote: my sweet spot is 100 bucks a month. If that was 100 bucks a month, I would have signed up to try it out, especially because it's not a subscription, it's just a month-to-month thing, right?... Do you guys have any promotions coming up? Father's Day or whatever is coming up next month?
objections.rep_response: Declined — 'We don't' — then asked how he would judge whether it was worth $100, $200 or $300. The prospect corrected him: it is a budget constraint, not a value judgement. Rep closed with an offer to notify him of any future promotions.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: For the one-month option: 'At the end of that month, if you decide to stay with us, you just pay the difference for three or six. If you're not really enjoying it, you just part ways there and shake hands as friends.' For Primal University: 'you're not committed to anything. You can cancel that at any time.'

evidence: The rep disqualified him explicitly: 'If you were to really, like, put gun to my head, I don't really think you need the one-on-one coaching like that... Some people aren't the best fit for this'
The prospect also declined on price twice — first the coaching tiers ('way out of my range') and then the $200 per month fallback ('my sweet spot is 100 bucks a month')
No payment, no link, no deposit, no follow-up call booked
Rep closed with an open door only: 'We're always going to be here. We're not going to shut the door. If there are any future promotions, I'll let you know'
Counter-evidence: genuine and stated intent to buy at a lower price — 'if there's any promotion that comes around 100 bucks, I'll frickin' jump on it at that same moment'
Counter-evidence: he rated trust in the programme seven to eight out of ten before the price was mentioned
outcome.next_step: None scheduled. Rep undertook to contact him if a promotion becomes available.

notable.note: The one call in this batch where the rep disqualified a prospect rather than discounting his way to a sale, and it was the right call — a $150 per month budget against a $4,000 minimum is not a gap that a payment plan closes. Worth holding up against the Brandon Johnson call the previous day, where a prospect in bankruptcy proceedings was walked down four price points to a close. Two things to escalate. First, the rep stated 'It's not a subscription model that we run here' at 00:25:01 and then, ten minutes later in the same call, offered a $200 per month product that 'you can cancel at any time'. Second, having disqualified the prospect, the rep volunteered that he runs his own fitness coaching business alongside this role: 'I do what I'm doing now with a few other businesses, consult, mainly in the fitness space. I have my own fitness coaching that I'm doing here as well.' Also notable that he could not demonstrate the $200 product he was selling — 'I can't show anything' — and the prospect said afterwards 'I'm still kind of figuring out what exactly it provides or not.'

quality.notes: Swapping is present but noticeably less severe than elsewhere in this batch, mostly on short turns and question-answer boundaries — for example at 00:07:17 the rep's question 'How long have you been on this fitness journey for yourself?' appears under the prospect. Long passages are correctly attributed, which makes this the most reliable transcript in the batch. Roles resolved from content. The prospect is not named in the file title, which reads only 'Impromptu Zoom Meeting', so this sales call is invisible to any title-driven process; his name was recovered from the rep addressing him throughout.
